headline: Brent broke 4.5% and the inflation composite still got worse — the input is rolling faster than the price of the inflation it caused.
summary: The energy premium cracked. Brent fell 4.5% to 110.08 while WTI gave up only 1.3% to 101.43 — Brent fell more than three times as hard, which is a physical/geopolitical premium coming out, not demand dying. Gasoline is the confirmation: -3.5% today and -6.6% on the month against WTI +13.5% on the month, a crack spread collapsing in real time. And yet the inflation composite deteriorated again, from -49 to -50, still the worst number on the board. The 5-year breakeven sits at 2.49%, +16bp on the month and turning up; the 30-year mortgage is pinned at 7.32% in the 94th percentile; DBC is in the 97.5th percentile and oil/gold at the 95th, +17.2% on the month. The bond market has not been paid back for one day of crude relief: 10y 5.05%, 30y 5.37%, real 2.67%, rates composite -35. That gap — crude rolling, breakevens not — is the cleanest asymmetry on the sheet today.

Yesterday's open question was the won. It answered. Korea gained 5.4% in the ETF and 3.1% in the index on Tuesday with USD/KRW going the wrong way; today KOSPI -1.2%, Taiwan -1.4%, and USD/KRW +0.8% to 1337.8. The squeeze did not survive 24 hours, and the KOSPI's month move is still a z=-1.94 at -13.6%. China is worse and quieter: Hang Seng -0.6% at the 5th percentile, Shanghai -0.8% at the 0.5th, KWEB -6.8% on the month, FXI -5.0% — all while USD/CNY fell to 6.6507, the 0th percentile of the year. A strengthening currency with collapsing equities is a deflation and capital-allocation signal, not a bullish one. The bid went to Europe and Japan instead: DAX +1.0% (+2.3% on the week), CAC +1.0%, Nikkei +1.1% (+2.8% on the week), Sensex +1.2% with acceleration 1.52.

Underneath, risk appetite is leaking in the places that lead. Crypto is the clearest tell: BTC -1.5% to 80,037 and -27.3% over a year, ETH -1.6% to 2,320 and -13.3% on the month, SOL -2.0% and -15.8% on the month, ETH/BTC -9.4% on the month, COIN at the 9.9th percentile. The S&P sits at the 95th percentile. Precious metals are being liquidated rather than sold on fundamentals — platinum -3.1% at the 0th percentile, silver 25.6% below its 200-day at the 8.6th, gold/silver +10.9% on the month at z=1.63 and accelerating +0.95 — while copper/gold holds the 98th percentile and copper is +3.6% on the week. Industrial demand is fine; the money is. The TGA is $1.0525tn, +11.3% on the month and at the 100th percentile, with RRP functionally empty at $0.18bn. The drain has no sponge, and the liquidity composite is a flat zero.

What hasn't changed is the quality of the leadership, and it is still rented. VIX 16.97 at the 20th percentile, VIX3M 19.22 at the 15th, term structure 0.88, MOVE -7.1% on the month — vol is cheap into a tape where the hardest accelerations are all defensive: SPLV +2.16, USMV +1.76, XLU +2.15 on a +8.3% month, MCD +2.58, HD +2.20. RSP/SPY posted the highest acceleration on the board at +2.46 and has still rolled over. Communications sit at the 0th percentile with META -14.4% on the month at acceleration -2.41 and NFLX at the 0th. The oddity worth a flag: LMT +21.6% on the month, z=2.80, the largest z-score anywhere on the sheet, while the broad defense ETF ITA is -12.0% over three months at the 18th percentile — that is single-name, not a war premium. Risk regime -11, a tick worse than yesterday's -10. Own convexity, not beta.
Brent -4.5% to 110.08 and gasoline -6.6% on the month finally put a dent in the single worst composite on the board (inflation, -50).

good.text: Crude's premium cracked: Brent -4.5% to 110.08 versus WTI -1.3% to 101.43, with gasoline -3.5% today and -6.6% on the month against WTI +13.5% — the primary input to the inflation composite is rolling.
Vol and credit remain inert: VIX 16.97 at the 20th percentile, VIX3M at the 15th, MOVE -7.1% on the month, BKLN at the 98.8th percentile and HYG/IEF +0.3%. Credit & vol composite +27.
The whole curve is lower on the month with decelerating upward momentum — 2y -25bp, 5y -21bp, 10y -19bp, 10y real -23bp, all with acceleration z around -2.
Leadership relocated to Europe, Japan and India: DAX +1.0% (+2.3% on the week, acc 0.95), Nikkei +1.1% (+2.8%), CAC +1.0%, Sensex +1.2% with acceleration 1.52.
Healthcare is the one sector with real, confirmed relative strength: XLV +4.9% on the month at the 96th percentile with RS turning up, IBB +2.0% at the 99th, LLY +8.7% at the 96th.
The dollar stopped pressing: DXY flat at 102.15 with acceleration -0.37, EUR +0.2%, USD/CAD -0.5%, USD/CNY -0.3% to 6.6507 — the 0th percentile of the year.

bad.text: Inflation composite worsened again to -50, the worst reading on the board: 5y breakeven 2.49% (+16bp on the month, turning up), 30y mortgage 7.32% at the 94th percentile, 30y yield 5.37%, 10y 5.05%.
The Korea squeeze failed in one session: KOSPI -1.2% after +7.3% on the week, Taiwan -1.4%, USD/KRW +0.8% to 1337.8. The currency non-confirmation flagged two days ago resolved bearishly.
China keeps bleeding with a strengthening currency — Hang Seng -0.6% at the 5th percentile, Shanghai -0.8% at the 0.5th, KWEB -6.8% and FXI -5.0% on the month. That is a deflation signal, not value.
Crypto is bleeding while the S&P sits at the 95th percentile: BTC -1.5% to 80,037, ETH -1.6% (-13.3% on the month), SOL -2.0% (-15.8%), ETH/BTC -9.4% on the month, COIN at the 9.9th percentile.

Precious metals are being liquidated: platinum -3.1% at the 0th percentile, silver 25.6% below its 200-day, gold/silver +10.9% on the month at z=1.63 and accelerating — a funding signal, since copper/gold is at the 98th percentile.

Breadth is fake and the plumbing is tight: RSP/SPY has rolled over despite acceleration +2.46, the hardest-accelerating factors are SPLV (2.16), USMV (1.76) and XLU (2.15), while the TGA is $1.0525tn at the 100th percentile and RRP is empty at $0.18bn.

trades.name: Fade the E&P extension into the crude break
trades.line: Short XOP: crude premium cracking, E&P 19% over its 200-day
trades.expr: Short XOP outright or December 195/175 put spread; keep a partial long in XOM/CVX as integrated hedge if you must stay sector-neutral.
trades.thesis: E&P equity has priced a $110 Brent world. Brent just fell 4.5% in a session while WTI fell 1.3% — the premium unwinding is in the physical barrel, and the crack spread already told you refining margins were gone (gasoline -6.6% on the month against WTI +13.5%). XOP is 18.8% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile with +10.3% one-month relative strength; that is where the pain is cheapest to inflict.
trades.trigger: Brent -4.5% to 110.08 today, gasoline -3.5% and -6.6% on the month, XOP +11.2% on the month with acceleration 0.97 into the 95th percentile.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 115 or WTI closes above 105; XOP makes a new high above 206.

trades.name: Short 5-year breakevens
trades.line: Short 5y breakevens into the Brent break
trades.expr: Sell 5y breakeven (short 5y TIPS vs long 5y nominal) at 2.49%; retail proxy is short a TIPS ETF against an equivalent-duration nominal Treasury position.
trades.thesis: The 5y breakeven is +16bp on the month, turning up, at z=0.7, and almost all of that move is crude. The crude move just reversed hard at the front of the barrel. Breakevens are the slowest leg of the inflation trade to reprice and the cheapest place to be contrarian while the long end stays stubborn.
trades.trigger: 5y breakeven 2.49% and the inflation composite at -50 on the same day Brent fell 4.5% and gasoline fell 3.5%; 10y breakeven only 2.38%, so the curve of inflation expectations is already hump-shaped at the front.
trades.stop: 5y breakeven trades above 2.60%, or Brent closes back above 115 with gasoline reclaiming its 200-day.
trades.target: 5y breakeven 2.30%, back to flat on the quarter.

trades.name: Long SMH / short EWY
trades.line: Long SMH vs short EWY: the won says the squeeze is over
trades.expr: Long SMH, short EWY, dollar-neutral at roughly 1:1 notional.
trades.thesis: Korea's +5.4% day was a short squeeze financed by a weakening currency, and it has already given back. You keep the silicon exposure where the cycle still works and short the leveraged, FX-exposed version of it. KOSPI's one-month move is z=-1.94 at -13.6% while SMH/SPY is turning up off a z=-1.2.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -1.2% and Taiwan -1.4% today with USD/KRW +0.8% to 1337.8, one session after EWY +5.4%; EWY relative strength is -10.4% over one month.
trades.stop: USD/KRW breaks below 1310 with KOSPI reclaiming its 200-day (currently 9.2% above spot).

trades.name: Buy index convexity
trades.line: Buy SPX convexity: VIX 17 with breadth rolling over
trades.expr: Buy December SPX 7500/7000 put spread, or January VIX 22/30 call spread; size to 40-60bp of premium.
trades.thesis: Vol is priced at the 15th-20th percentile of the year into a tape whose breadth has rolled over and whose fastest-accelerating components are low-vol, min-vol and utilities. A market that rallies while SPLV accelerates at +2.16 and RSP/SPY turns down at acceleration +2.46 is renting beta. Convexity is the cheapest expression of everything else on this page.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.97 at the 20th percentile and VIX3M at the 15th with term structure 0.88 and SKEW 148.74 turning up, while SPX sits at the 95th percentile and RSP/SPY has rolled over.
trades.stop: VIX breaks below 14 with RSP/SPY making a new high — i.e. breadth confirms the index.
trades.target: VIX above 24; 3x on the call spread, 2.5x on the put spread.

trades.name: Own healthcare and biotech
trades.line: Long IBB/XLV: leadership with real relative strength
trades.expr: Long IBB 60% / XLV 40%; add XBI on any pullback to its 200-day.
trades.thesis: This is the only group where price, relative strength and breadth agree. XLV is +4.9% on the month at the 96th percentile with relative strength turning up; IBB is at the 99th percentile, +14.8% over three months, with relative strength up on both windows. It works if growth slows and the long end finally follows crude lower, and it does not depend on the AI capex cycle that is rotating violently inside itself.
trades.trigger: IBB +2.0% and XBI +1.7% on the last print, XLV +4.9% on the month, LLY +8.7% at the 96th percentile and UNH +7.7% with relative strength turning up — leadership that broadened while XLC sat at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: IBB loses 200 (below its 50-day) or XLV relative strength turns down on the one-month window.

trades.name: Short Coinbase
trades.line: Short COIN: crypto bleeding while SPX sits at 95th pct
trades.expr: Short COIN outright or buy January 160/120 put spread.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the highest-beta read on retail risk appetite and it is decaying while the index makes highs — exactly the divergence that preceded past drawdowns in speculative beta. COIN carries the volume-decline and the equity-beta risk at once: -54.3% over twelve months, 9.9th percentile, rolling over, relative strength -16.1% on the month.
trades.trigger: BTC -1.5% to 80,037 (-27.3% y/y), ETH -1.6% and -13.3% on the month, SOL -15.8% on the month, ETH/BTC -9.4% — altcoin beta leading the complex lower on a day the S&P sits at the 95th percentile.
trades.stop: BTC reclaims 88,000 with IBIT making a new three-month high; COIN above 185.

trades.name: Short the gold/silver ratio
trades.line: Short gold/silver: z=1.63 liquidation, copper says no
trades.expr: Long SLV versus short GLD on equal dollar notional, or short the gold/silver ratio via futures (long 2 SI vs short 1 GC equivalent).
trades.thesis: A 10.9% one-month move in gold/silver at z=1.63 with acceleration +0.95 is a liquidation of leveraged silver length, not a demand signal. The industrial tell disagrees: copper is +3.6% on the week at the 89th percentile and copper/gold sits at the 98th. Silver at 25.6% below its 200-day and the 8.6th percentile is where forced selling ends, not where it begins.
trades.trigger: Gold/silver 76.4 and +10.9% on the month at the 81st percentile while platinum -3.1% at the 0th percentile — the whole white-metal complex liquidating in one week.
trades.stop: Ratio closes above 82, or copper breaks back below its 200-day (6.2%).
